issues.title: FSST DFA filter: lane-refill interleaving + absorbing-state early exit
issues.hypothesis: After E0042, q13 (261ms, 2nd slowest) still spends 1.23s CPU in the orders scan (profile.md). Measured hot with dbe-tool sql: `count(*) WHERE o_comment NOT LIKE '%unusual%packages%'` takes 172ms wall / 1.35s user, and `NOT LIKE '%zq%'` (a 2-state DFA) takes 161ms. A full FSST decode of all 15M strings is cheaper: `WHERE o_comment <> 'abc'` takes 84ms and `sum(length(o_comment))` 88ms. So the code-level DFA is about 2x slower than decoding, even though it writes nothing. The cause is the loop in FSSTStorage::Filter (fsst.cpp:1114-1151). It groups 4 strings, runs the 4 interleaved chains only up to the SHORTEST length (`common`), then finishes each string's tail serially (`for k = common..lens[l]`). o_comment lengths vary widely (about 19-78 chars, so roughly 8-35 codes), so most codes run on a single dependent chain, `s = table[s + code]`, at about 6 cycles per code (L1 load latency plus the add). That is about 3ns/code, which matches 375M codes / 1.3s. Also, nothing exits early when the DFA reaches an absorbing state (the 'dead' state of a failed anchor, or 'done' when an unanchored-end pattern has matched). So a prefix pattern like 'forest%' or a contains of a common word still walks every code.
issues.plan: Only the inner loop and pattern init in src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp change. (1) In the FSST scan state's pattern initialisation (InitializePattern, around fsst.cpp:768-790, where pattern_table and pattern_accept are built), also compute per state whether it is absorbing: every one of the 256 code transitions, including the escape states, returns to the same state. FSSTPatternDFA::Build already creates explicit `done`/`dead` states (fsst.cpp:654-671), so this can simply be taken from there. Store it as a bit in pattern_accept (for example bit 1), or as a parallel vector indexed by s>>8. (2) Replace the 4-group loop (fsst.cpp:1114-1151) with a K-lane scheduler, K=8 (try 6/8/12). Each lane holds (cur ptr, end ptr, state, row). Each iteration advances every active lane by one code; this is the hot path with independent chains. When a lane reaches its end, or (checked every code or every few codes) enters an absorbing state, record accept for its row and refill the lane from the next candidate in sel. Rows that finish early must still land in new_sel in ascending order. Simplest: write a per-candidate pass/fail byte array indexed by candidate position i, then compact into new_sel in a final loop. Drain the remaining lanes at the end. Keep the escape-code handling exactly as it is now (escape states are ordinary table states, so it is unchanged). (3) Optional, measure separately: a speculative fast path for state 0 of unanchored patterns, `s = s ? table[s+c] : table0[c]`, which breaks the data dependency through branch prediction while the DFA sits in its start state. Micro A/B with .timer: NOT LIKE '%unusual%packages%', NOT LIKE '%zq%', LIKE '%unusual%packages%', contains(o_comment,'the'), and prefix-only LIKE 'ab%' on o_comment. Goal: below the 84ms decode baseline. Correctness: compare counts against the `o_comment||''` reference for the same pattern set the E0042 implementer used, including multi-%, anchors, NOT, escape-coded bytes, and candidate rows already narrowed by a previous filter.
issues.expected_gain: q13: the scan accounts for about 170ms of a 261ms query. If the DFA reaches about 2x throughput (1.35s -> about 0.6s CPU), q13 drops to about 190-210ms (-20..-25%), roughly -1.5..-2% geomean. Templates without LIKE on FSST columns: 0.
issues.generality: Every LIKE/NOT LIKE/contains/prefix/suffix scan filter on an FSST VARCHAR column (comments, names, addresses). Early exit helps prefix-anchored patterns most (q20-style p_name LIKE 'forest%': dead after 1-2 codes) and contains on common words. Nothing changes for Dictionary/DictFSST/uncompressed columns. Worst case: very short strings, where lane-refill bookkeeping per string could cost more than it saves; o_comment and p_name are 20-80 chars.
issues.risk: Low-medium. One function plus an init-time flag, with no plan or plumbing changes. Correctness risk: rows reaching new_sel out of order, or lost lane state at the drain. Both are caught by count comparisons against the ||'' reference.

## Memory (gen3)

## State
- gen1: accepted JoinDependent rule order (q19), contains() selectivity (q09), perfect HJ RIGHT (q13), BF first key multi-key HJ (q09), key-set range filter through compress projs (q18), exact bitmap BF, semi-join estimate, OR-of-ranges mask, FSST simple decode + substring prefilter (q13), DELIM_GET-build BF (q22). Best 1.281x.
- gen2: E0021 deliminate SEMI + exact BF through CM offset; E0022 exact-BF small-range floor; E0023 ANTI deliminator; E0024 parallel perfect-HJ build; E0027 BitPacking per-value select + exact BF 2^27; E0029 sparse perfect-HJ exact BF; E0031 block cache 256MB + large perfect HA v3. Best 1.800x.
- gen3 r1-r4: E0033 clustered-key agg, E0034 staged perfect HA sink, E0035 parallel HJ finalize 64K-1M, E0036 streaming run agg: all ACCEPTED. Best 2.120x.
- gen3 r5-r7: E0037 partition-local HJ slots RETIRED; E0039 THP v2 ACCEPTED (HugePageUtil, huge_page_util.hpp).
- gen3 r8: E0040 coalesce sparse scan chunks ACCEPTED. r9: E0041 caching threshold RETIRED.
- gen3 r10: E0042 FSST DFA LIKE filter v2 ACCEPTED (geomean -3.3%, q13 -24%). Best 2.468x.
- gen3 r11: DISPATCHED "FSST DFA filter: lane-refill interleaving + absorbing-state early exit".
- Backlog issues.md is mostly STALE: Length-aware sel, Perfect HJ RIGHT, Join min/max+BF through CM, Large perfect HA v3, RIGHT_SEMI/ANTI filters, FSST code-level LIKE v1: ALL LANDED. Live: "Skip unused local table in staged perfect HA" (small), "Skip agg CM compress" (q13; risky, CM fold had no gain).

## FSST DFA facts (r11 measurements, hot, dbe-tool sql .timer)
- orders o_comment (15M rows): NOT LIKE '%unusual%packages%' 172ms/1.35s user; NOT LIKE '%zq%' 161ms; LIKE '%unusual%packages%' 104ms; contains 'the' 147ms; `<> 'abc'` (full decode) 84ms; sum(length) 88ms; plain int filter 14ms.
- So the DFA is SLOWER than decoding. Cause: fsst.cpp FSSTStorage::Filter (~:1114) uses 4-string groups up to the min length, then a serial tail per string: a dependent-load chain at ~3ns/code. No absorbing-state early exit.
- Non-NOT rare patterns (contains 'zq', '%zzz') take ~87ms, probably skipped by the substring prefilter. NOT patterns don't use the prefilter.
- If lane-refill is retired for noise: rerun q13 alone (noise ~14%). If it is a bad implementation (micro A/B shows no gain), try the speculative state-0 path instead.
- o_comment = plain FSST (977 segs, ~15K rows each) + Constant validity. Fast path needs NULL-free segments and a single compression type per column.

## q09 breakdown (r11, hot wall, cumulative prefixes)
- lineitem⋈part(BF) 86ms; +partsupp 134ms; +orders 225-244ms (HJ build 3.27M wide lineitem-side rows, probe 2.9M orders = biggest step, ~90ms); +supplier+nation+group by n_name 310-345ms.
- Grouping by n_nationkey instead of n_name saves only ~28ms (q09 284 vs 312), so the string group key is worth ~10% of q09 at most.
- The EXPLAIN ANALYZE operator timings (profile.md / dbe-tool profile) are heavily inflated: lineitem scan shows 3.96s while the real wall of that whole piece is 86ms. Trust .timer A/B over operator timings.

## q03 (131ms)
- Orders⋈customer side 35ms; lineitem scan (shipdate filter + exact BF l_orderkey) + probe ~85ms. The scan uses AdaptiveFilter (scan_state.cpp:59), so filter order is already adaptive.

## Per-chunk overhead (E0040 lesson)
- Sparse chunks cost ~3.5us/chunk in HJ probe. HJ ExecuteInternal is called twice per input chunk (small follow-up).

## THP facts
- Free-time MADV_DONTNEED + MADV_NOHUGEPAGE REQUIRED, or q02 +5..9%.

## Profiling trick
- dbe-tool profile <instance> (e.g. q09.m0); pipe to grep -E 'rows|[0-9]s |...' (only single pipes to grep are allowed, not sed/awk).
- JSON profiling via PRAGMA + read_text regexp works too. `.timer on` as the first line. `SET disabled_optimizers='...'` for A/B. `col||''` disables filter pushdown (reference).

## Refuted (don't retry)
- VARCHAR low-card group key (q09 prior run); partition-local HJ slots; q05 join order; operator caching threshold; skipping CM wholesale; scan filter cost order (adaptive already).

## HJ / perfect facts
- PARALLEL_CONSTRUCT_THRESHOLD = 64K. ScanStructure::Next join_hashtable.cpp:940. Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp. Perfect HA: perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp, plan_aggregate.cpp. Exact BF: bloom_filter.cpp TemplatedLookupExact.

## Acceptance lessons
- Acceptance needs a template faster beyond noise AND a better geomean; any template slower beyond noise retires the change.
- Bundling or widening a near miss works (E0021, E0027, E0029, E0031, E0039).
- Full-bench single-template outliers of ±8..29% happen; rerun alone.

## Codebase facts
- Table scan: table_scan.cpp TableScanFunc. CachingPhysicalOperator: physical_operator.cpp:287-470.
- HJ BF filled in JoinHashTable::InsertHashes. BitPacking Select ~bitpacking.cpp:886. TEMP tables are never compressed.
- Substring prefilter: column_segment.cpp:662-860. CM: src/optimizer/compressed_materialization*. Deliminator: deliminator.cpp.
- FSST filter: fsst.cpp FSSTPatternDFA (:535), InitializePattern (~:770), Filter (:1081). Filter-only flag: ScanFilter::filter_only / ColumnScanState::filter_only. Piecewise straddle: standard_column_data.cpp.

## How to measure
- Bench noise: q16 ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%, q14 ~5.1%, q05 ~20%, q04 ~20%, q07 ~13%.

## Profile snapshot (r11): q09 307, q13 261, q18 247, q16 157, q03 131, q07 128, q05 122, q04 107, q08 106, q22 95, q17 92, q19 86, q14 83, q02 54. Geomean 125.6ms.

## Dead / exhausted
- CM join-key removal, HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ (8M range), hashed BF through CM offset, q13 eager aggregation, fused hashed BF probe, allocator flush thresholds, substring search alone, private staging for perfect HA, partition-local HJ slots, q05 join order, operator output caching threshold.

## Next candidates
1. FSST DFA lane-refill (dispatched r11). Follow-up: NULL-segment support for the FSST filter; projected-column straddle.
2. q09 orders HJ: 3.27M wide build rows (~90ms wall step). Investigate build sink vs finalize vs probe split with .timer variants (narrow payload).
3. q18 per-group streaming-run overhead (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp SinkInteriorRuns ~947).
4. String group key (q09 ~10% max; only 1-column dictionary groups are handled, aggregate_hashtable.cpp:359).
5. HJ double call per input chunk (small). Skip unused local table in staged perfect HA (q13 -1..-3%).
